newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam first-half oil output up yr-on-yr 18.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam first-half oil output up yr-on-yr 18.5 pct.

text.p: State oil and gas firm Petrovietnam and its production-sharing partners pumped a record 4.87 million tonnes of crude oil in the first six months of this year, the official Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said on Tuesday.
The first-half output, most of which came from the Vietnamese-Russian joint venture Vietsovpetro, was 18.5 percent higher than in the same period of 1996.

"With a daily output of 26,900 tonnes of crude at the White Tiger (Bach Ho), Dragon (Rong) and Big Bear (Dai Hung) oilfields, Petrovietnam is expected to tap the 50-millionth tonne by the end of August and exceed the yearly target of nine million tonnes," VNA said.
Last year's production was 8.805 million tonnes, 15 percent of which came from production-sharing projects with foreign partners.
Separately, the General Statistics Office said Vietnam's crude oil exports in the first six months of this year came to 4.6 million tonnes, a year-on-year increase of 13.6 percent.
VNA said Petrovietnam had also pumped more than 200 million cubic metres of associated gas to the Ba Ria and Phu My thermo-electric plants since the beginning of this year.
It added that the company had completed the installation of a new gas pipeline and was aiming to supply three million cubic metres of gas a day to the two plants by mid-August.
Vietnam is planning to increase its gross oil equivalent production to between 30 milliom and 40 million tonnes by 2010, with gas output at six to seven billion cubic metres a year.
